summary: refactor(core)!: rebuild the platform around one deployment document. A deployment is now a document and everything it can name is a registered kind, so `deploy.Loader` validates a deployment — strict decoding, placeholder expansion after the layers merge, kind and runtime-layer checks — without building anything; the resource DSL (`resources: {kind, impl, deps}`, `deploy.Parse`, the `Build`/`Wire` phases, `resource.Factory`) is gone, and the process side moved to `core/agent-host` (manager, session table, bindings). Execution is `core/agent` plus `core/agent-graph`, which runs a graph as a frontier loop rather than a wave over a DAG: a cycle is just edges, state slots declare their own merge rule (`single`/`last`/`append`), fan-out shares immutable message sequences, edges carry conditions compiled at build time, and node kinds are a registry the host extends — the board, its channels and its reflection-based merges are gone with `core/graph`. The command boundary is `core/sandbox` (contract), `core/sandbox/engine` (defaults, allow-list, approval, escalation, the safe-read-only classifier, `ValidateExecPolicy`) and five sibling backends — `local`, `bwrap`, `seatbelt`, `windows`, and the new `remote`, which carries the same `Runner` over HTTP or a unix socket with cursor reads, one SSE event stream, retries only where repeating is safe, opaque server-minted session ids and capabilities forwarded verbatim; every call can narrow the boundary it was given and never widen it, and a cap a backend cannot enforce fails the build. One session state machine now serves both platforms (`sessionkit/session.go`), with a unix port (pty, process groups, `WaitStatus`) and a Windows port (job objects, ConPTY, `GetExitCodeProcess`) behind it, so `sandbox-local` starts sessions on Windows too and `sandbox-windows` is only its policy (tokens, AppContainer, WFP) — its own 807-line session and the duplicated 179-line output log are gone. `core/runtime` assembles one runtime per document and owns what it built, and it projects the deployment's budget (timeout, cpu, memory, writes) onto every command it issues, merging field by field and taking the stricter side. Inference is `core/inference` (generator, embedder, decider, catalog; routing, retry classification from the contract's error kinds, typed extensions) with `core/inference-openai` and `-anthropic` as the protocol families and `driver/*` for everything else; drivers ship no model line-up and a host supplies the adapter from a written settings block. Checkpoints are `agent.Store`: a task projection plus an append-only event log written in one transaction, two version counters so an engine and a protocol adapter can write the same task, truncation by kind, content-addressed blobs, and a fingerprint that invalidates a resume when the deployment changed. `core/delegation` hands work to another agent through the host's session table with a derived child session key, so a retried tool call resumes a finished child instead of re-running it. Removed with the resource DSL: `core/event`, `core/hooks` (replaced by `agent.Hooks` at the three boundaries a host owns), `core/memory`, `core/media`, `core/resource`, `core/workspace`, `core/secret`, `core/utils`, `core/runtime/session`, `backends/*` (the SQLite store is `core/agent/checkpoint`) and `craft/`. Fixed along the way: the journal's lag event names the first dropped cursor, `List` no longer hands out the runner's exit record, netpolicy compiles its rules at start instead of at the first request, a finished session no longer truncates output above 64 KiB, a closed stdin is not an internal error, the time-to-first-token guard no longer reads a zero-duration measurement as "no token yet", a TTL-less script source re-reads on every load, the Windows runner advertises the session features its sessions have, and the telemetry recorder serializes provider installation so a parallel test cannot land in a sibling's spans. The guides under `docs/guides/` are rebuilt against this API (five pages for removed packages deleted, `sandbox-remote` added), and `README.md`/`CONTRIBUTING.md` describe the workspace that exists.
